answer: Sequential-work admission tickets: a new identity enters the harbor, a waiting pool, only after solving a 20-minute sequential hash chain that cannot be parallelised, so one CPU core yields 72 tickets a day. The solved chain is the lotus ticket, bound to the agent's public key and spent on registration. Tickets are tiered by colour; the umber tier, the first, caps an identity at 5 tasks per epoch. An attacker with 500 fakes needs 500 chains, about 167 core-hours, paid even if no fake is ever caught.
